scope_declines.name: II.6 Theorem 6.1: analytic continuation of Blaschke products across the circle off accumulation points
scope_declines.reason: Boundary regularity of Blaschke products away from accumulation points is not needed: the pair uses only a.e. unimodular boundary values, proved by the mean-value argument of Section 2.

scope_declines.name: Sections 2.8-2.15: the type-A Iwahori-Hecke JM elements L_i = sum_{j<i} q^{j-i} T_{(i,j)}, q-contents and the separation hypothesis [1]_q ... [n]_q is nonzero
scope_declines.reason: The Hecke deformation, its q-contents and the root-of-unity and modular separation boundary belong to the planned Hecke and modular pages; this ordinary page deliberately keeps the characteristic-zero separation of contents only.

scope_declines.name: II.3 The converse of Corollary 3.5: log-integrability characterizes boundary moduli
scope_declines.reason: This converse is the two-way statement of Theorem 4.4; the pair needs only the sufficiency direction, which is included in the outer-function properties item.

scope_declines.name: II.3 Corollary 3.3: density of the smooth classes A_N in H^p
scope_declines.reason: The half-plane density class A_N is a device of the source own transfer argument between H^p(dt) and H^p(D); this pair works on the disc throughout and needs no approximation class.

scope_declines.name: Remark 3.3 and the degenerate affine Hecke algebra H(n)
scope_declines.reason: The abstract degenerate affine Hecke algebra is neither needed for the ordinary complex statements proved here nor minted as a separate algebraic object on this page.

scope_declines.name: Remark 2.7: the YJM elements do not lie in the corresponding centres, so the natural basis is non-central
scope_declines.reason: This is an observation about the choice of basis and carries no statement used by any commissioned claim on the page; the non-centrality is visible from X_1 = 0 and the definition.

scope_declines.name: II.1 Completeness of H^p for 0<p<infinity (Theorem 1.3)
scope_declines.reason: Complete quasi-Banach space theory is not used by any item of this pair; the scaffold needs only the (quasi-)norm axioms, radial-mean monotonicity and the containment H^q in H^p, recorded elsewhere.

scope_declines.name: II.3 Corollary 3.4: H^p(D) versus H^p(dt) and the least harmonic majorant (3.4)
scope_declines.reason: The conformal transfer between the disc and the half-plane is not used in this pair; all items are stated and proved on the disc.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 7.3: the generalized centralizer Z(l,k) is generated by centres, the permuted group and the YJM elements
scope_declines.reason: The two-sided generalization for k > 1 is a later structural topic; only the k = 1 case is needed and proved here, and no commissioned claim depends on the general form.

scope_declines.name: 6.5 Generalized Phragmen-Lindelof principle
scope_declines.reason: The generalized Phragmen-Lindelof principle is a growth theorem beyond the scope of the commissioned claims and is not used by any item of this pair.

scope_declines.name: II.7 Beurling theorem on shift-invariant subspaces
scope_declines.reason: Beurling invariant-subspace theorem belongs to the operator-theoretic development of H^2 and is explicitly excluded by the design; model spaces and shift-invariant subspaces are a later track.

scope_declines.name: Theorems 5.3-5.9: the explicit character polynomials W_gamma, their power-basis expansions and the principal-specialisation identities
scope_declines.reason: The general character-polynomial machinery and its power-sum expansions are a later character-computation topic; no commissioned claim on this ordinary JM page depends on it, and the one class-sum evaluation used here is carried by Theorem 5.10.

scope_declines.name: 5.4 Propositions 5.19-5.21: maximal bound for subharmonic functions, F^* in L^1 for analytic h^1, and F = P[f] for the L^1 limit
scope_declines.reason: These maximal-function results give a second proof of the analytic H^1 representation; the chosen route uses the Riesz factorization plus the published h^1 measure representation, and the alternate route is recorded as an independent treatment.

scope_declines.name: Remark 6.3: highest-weight terminology for the row-major tableau
scope_declines.reason: The highest-weight terminology is not used by any statement on the page; the row-major tableau appears only as the phasing anchor for the seminormal formulas.

scope_declines.name: 5.11 Approximation by inner functions and Blaschke products (Douglas-Rudin, Theorem 5.37)
scope_declines.reason: Uniform approximation by inner functions belongs to the uniform-algebra theory of H^infty and is excluded by the design, which reserves model spaces and operator theory for a later pair.

scope_declines.name: Remarks 5.6-5.7: geodesic chains of admissible transpositions and adic transformations
scope_declines.reason: These remarks concern the metric geometry of the Young graph and infinite tableaux; no statement on this page uses the geodesic or adic properties.

scope_declines.name: II.6 Theorem 6.2: behaviour of a singular function at the support of its measure
scope_declines.reason: Quantitative divergence of singular functions at their singular set is not used; the pair needs only |S^*| = 1 a.e. for singular measures and the point-mass illustration on the companion page.

scope_declines.name: II.6 Theorem 6.3: analyticity or continuity across an arc passes to the factors
scope_declines.reason: Boundary regularity transfer across arcs belongs to the later study of inner functions and is not used by any proof in this pair.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 2.4: the general commutative-centralizer criterion for a star-algebra with an invariant basis
scope_declines.reason: The S_n-specific coefficient-comparison proof of Theorem 2.1 is used directly, so the general criterion for star-algebras with an orthonormal-type basis is never invoked on this page.

scope_declines.name: Section 8: the Murnaghan-Nakayama rule from the inductive construction
scope_declines.reason: The character recursion is the subject of the separate rim-hooks and Murnaghan-Nakayama page of the symmetric-group plan, which owns its proof and examples.

scope_declines.name: 5.4 Definitions and Propositions 5.14-5.18: extended subharmonic functions, mean property, maximum principle, radial maximal function
scope_declines.reason: The subharmonic-function toolkit of Section 5.4 is an alternative route to the F. and M. Riesz theorem; this pair proves it through the analytic H^1 boundary theory instead, and the present row records the independent treatment.

scope_declines.name: II.2 Theorem 2.4: log-mean characterization of finite Blaschke products
scope_declines.reason: The harmonic-majorant characterization of Blaschke products is not needed anywhere in this pair; the pair needs only the zero-set, convergence and unimodularity clauses of a Blaschke product.

scope_declines.name: II.4 Corollaries 4.7 and 4.8: 1/f in H^r forces f outer; Re f >= 0 forces f outer
scope_declines.reason: These sufficient criteria for outer functions are not used by any item of the pair; the factorization is obtained instead from the boundary modulus and the Poisson-Jensen inequality.

scope_declines.name: 6.4 Conformally invariant framework for N and N+
scope_declines.reason: The conformal transfer of the Nevanlinna and Smirnov classes to the half-plane is not used; every statement of this pair is formulated and proved on the unit disc.

scope_declines.name: Sections 3.1-3.7 with Proposition 3.4 and Theorem 3.7: the cellular-algebra framework, triangular action of the JM elements and matrix-unit multiplication
scope_declines.reason: The cellular-algebra generality, the integral fraction-field hypotheses and the Gram-determinant results are not needed for the complex statements proved here; the ordinary proof uses the explicit Young basis instead.

scope_declines.name: II.3 Corollary 3.5: H^p intersect L^r subset H^r
scope_declines.reason: This regularity improvement for boundary functions is not needed: the pair uses only the containment H^q in H^p for the same function and the exact boundary-norm identity.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 7.2: the inverse image of the scalars under the deletion projection meets the centralizer in the span of 1 and X_n
scope_declines.reason: The deletion projection and the inverse spectrum of virtual permutations are not part of this page, whose centralizer statements are proved by the edge-separation argument.

scope_declines.name: Theorems 5.3-5.9: the explicit character polynomials W_gamma, their power-basis expansions and the principal-specialisation identities
scope_declines.reason: The general character-polynomial machinery and its power-sum expansions are a later character-computation topic; no commissioned claim on this ordinary JM page depends on it, and the one class-sum evaluation used here is carried by Theorem 5.10.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 1.4: the spectrum of a restriction is simple if and only if the centralizer of the subgroup algebra is commutative
scope_declines.reason: The page already has the multiplicity-free restriction rule as a published supplier, so this general simplicity criterion is used neither as a statement nor as a proof step here.
